newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Plutonic says in new gold discovery.
newsitem.headline: Plutonic says in new gold discovery.

text.p: Plutonic Resources Ltd said on Thursday it has made a significant gold discovery near its Darlot gold mine in Western Australia.

"The great thickness of the mineralised zone, its high grade and it apparent continuity over a width of at least 160 metres indicate, even at this early stage of testing, that a large mineable gold deposit has been discovered," Plutonic said.
Plutonic said the discovery, named Darlot Centenary, is open laterally in all directions.
If appreciable lateral extensions are proven a "very substantial gold deposit will be defined," it said.
The vertical step-out drill hole number 362, located 1.2 km east of the existing Darlot gold pit, recently interesected a previously unknown gold mineralised zone, the company said.

The intersections returned results of 33 metres at 8.0 grams of gold per tonne of ore from 332 metres, 10 metres at 5.2 grams/t from 332 metres and 14 metres at 15.2 grams/t from 351 metres, Plutonic said.

Follow-up drilling of a second hole returned results of 59 metres at 6.6 grams/t from 355 metres, including 25 metres at 5.8 grams/t from 355 metres, 15 metres at 13.0 grams/t from 380 metres and 19 metres at 2.6 grams/t from 395 metres, Plutonic said.
Denis Clarke, Plutonic's corporate general manager, said that if a decision is made to proceeed to development of the deposit, work could get started in a short period.
"The (grade) thickness is so good that you are not going to have to hum and haw about the economics of it, as they are painfully obvious," Clarke told Reuters.
Clarke said the new desposit should be interpreted geologically as a separate gold zone from its Darlot mine.
"I don't want people to say the boys have just been drilling out from the Darlot deposit, just extending it," Clarke said.
"This is potentially several times larger than the existing Darlot deposit," he said.
The Darlot mine produced 400,000 ounces from open cut mining, which ended in 1995,
The mine was subsequently transformed to an underground operation.
In the June quarter, Darlot produced 17,355 ounces Plutonic said.
